extracted.intended_audience: NASA SMD Program Officers, Reviewers (panel and external), Panel Chairs, and Selection Officials involved in Research & Analysis peer review and selection
extracted.subtask_description: Policy-level requirements and standards for conducting peer review and selection of Research & Analysis (R&A) proposals within NASA's Science Mission Directorate, covering roles, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, panel evaluations, ratings, timing, and selection documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subject matter experts (SMEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science Mission Directorate (SMD) uses peer review by subject matter experts (SMEs) to evaluate proposals submitted to the Directorate in response to a NASA Research Announcement (NRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMEs evaluate proposals using appropriate factors to assess evaluation criteria; applied across SMD R&A programs to ensure consistent, high-quality reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation according to appropriate factors/evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: SMD uses input from SMEs to evaluate proposals using appropriate factors to assess evaluation criteria (e.g., intrinsic merit, cost reasonableness, programmatic relevance; see Guidebook for Proposers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officers shall ensure evaluation criteria used during the Panel Review are the same as those described in the solicitation and that reviewers apply the criteria uniformly and hold all proposals to the same standards (§4.2.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent, unconflicted, respectful, inclusive, timely reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: SMD places high value on the competent, unconflicted, respectful, inclusive, and timely review of all compliant and responsive proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must be competent and free from conflicts; Program Officers must invite competent reviewers and make best efforts to ensure diversity (§3.4.5, §3.4.6, §3.1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of proposals and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: SMD protects the confidentiality of proposers and reviewers as well as the sensitive and proprietary content of submitted proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reviewers shall keep the entire Peer Review confidential; federal employees governed by 41 U.S.C 423; non-federal reviewers must sign a Nondisclosure Agreement before access to full proposals (§3.1.1, §4.1.2, §3.4.3). Review materials and notes must be destroyed at end of panel meeting (§4.2.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer authority and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: SMD entrusts its Program Officers to implement its policies and practices and present well-supported selection recommendations to the Selection Officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Program Officer has responsibility and authority for all aspects of the Peer Review and is accountable to the Selection Official; certain inherently governmental activities must be performed or approved by civil servants or IPAs (§3.4, §3.4.5, §3.4.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Official responsibility to advance strategic goals
rubrics_metrics.description: SMD entrusts its Selection Officials to advance its strategic goals and maximize science return within programmatic constraints when making selection decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection Officials make final selection decisions and must document rationales in selection documents; Program Officers present Selection Recommendations (§3.5, §4.5.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and separation of review types (individual, panel, external)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review processes distinguish Individual Reviews (single reviewer, produced without discussion), Panel Evaluation (non-consensus consolidated compilation informed by discussion), Individual Rating, and Panel Rating (median of Individual Ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Ratings should be the median of Individual Ratings of unconflicted panel reviewers; procedures for aggregation are specified (§2.1, §4.3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer obligation: report real or perceived conflicts of interest or bias
rubrics_metrics.description: All Reviewers shall alert the Program Officer of any real or perceived conflicts of interest or bias in their participation in the discussion or evaluation of any proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must self-identify conflicts; federal employees must complete a Self Certification Form (see SPD-16) (§3.1.2, §4.1.1). Program Officers must follow documented standards for eliminating or mitigating conflicts (§3.4.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer obligation: provide competent, unconflicted, unbiased Individual Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: All Reviewers shall provide Individual Reviews that are competent, unconflicted, and unbiased. Panel Reviewers shall also familiarize themselves with all the proposals before the Review Panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Reviewers must review all proposals assigned to the panel unless prevented by conflict (§3.1.3, §3.2.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to applicable code(s) of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: All Reviewers shall agree and adhere to any applicable code(s) of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officers and Panel Chairs shall uphold applicable codes of conduct; Program Officers shall ensure the peer review is conducted in accordance with any applicable codes (§3.1.4, §3.3.2, §3.4.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When serving as Primary Reviewer, lead the discussion and drafting of the Panel Evaluation; work with the Program Officer to ensure the Panel Evaluation reflects the panel discussion and is informative to NASA and the proposer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary Reviewer must approve Panel Evaluations; Panel Evaluations shall incorporate relevant findings from Individual Reviews (§3.2.1, §4.3.1, §4.3.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When serving as the Secondary Reviewer, actively participate in the panel discussion and assist the Primary Reviewer in drafting the Panel Evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary Reviewer participates in discussions and helps produce Panel Evaluation content (§3.2.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Reviewer participation in discussions and independent ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Reviewers shall participate in discussions of, and provide Independent Ratings for, all proposals before the Review Panel, unless prevented by a real or perceived conflict of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent Ratings inform Panel Ratings; Panel Ratings are medians of Individual Ratings from unconflicted reviewers (§3.2.3, §4.3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Chair duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Panel Chair shall shepherd discussions so the Review Panel stays on topic and on schedule; aid the Program Officer in upholding codes of conduct; ensure the Panel Evaluations and Ratings reflect the Review Panel’s discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Chair helps ensure timely, orderly discussion and that evaluations accurately capture panel outcomes (§3.3.1–3.3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer: follow SMD policies and federal regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Officer shall follow all applicable SMD policies and practices during the Peer Review, which in turn ensures compliance with all applicable Federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Appendix A for applicable documents (GCAM, NPR 1080.1, SPD series, etc.) (§3.4.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer: documented standards for handling conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow documented standards for eliminating or mitigating all real or perceived conflicts of interest or bias in the Peer Review processes; ensure records exist of the handling of any real or perceived conflicts within the Review Panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See SPD-01, SPD-05, SPD-16, SPD-40, SP-2018-371, NPR 1080.1, GCAM for procedures; final invitations to reviewers must be made or approved by a Civil Servant or IPA (§3.4.2, §3.4.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer: ensure confidentiality of the Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the entire Peer Review is kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality requirements include nondisclosure agreements and destruction of notes; Program Officer must brief and enforce confidentiality (§3.4.3, §4.2.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: deliver Selection Decisions within 150 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the Peer Review in a timely manner, with Selection Decisions (or an update) delivered to proposers within 150 days after the proposal due date (or submission date, in the case of no-due-date programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not delivered within 150 days, Program Officer shall provide status notifications to proposers with conservative estimates every 60 days until Selection Decisions are delivered (§3.4.4, §4.4.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer: appoint competent, unconflicted Reviewers and eliminate other conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint all Reviewers and ensure they are competent to evaluate their assigned proposals as well as free from any statutory and organizational conflicts of interest; eliminate any other known conflicts of interest (e.g., scientific, ethical) or bias that would prevent Reviewers from providing (or appearing to provide) fair evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decisions to invite Reviewers must be made or approved by a Civil Servant or IPA (§3.4.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer: invite reviewers reflecting diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that best efforts are made to invite Reviewers that reflect the diversity of the science community and ultimately the nation, in line with NASA’s core value of inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity across career stage, institution type, demographics, etc., should be considered in reviewer selection (§3.4.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer: provide reviewers access to necessary documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure Reviewers are well equipped to construct their reviews and participate in the Review Panel by providing timely access to all necessary documents, instructions, and descriptions of roles and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents include all proposals within the panel, ROSES Summary of Solicitation, relevant appendices, Guidebook for Proposers, and any applicable codes of conduct (§4.1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of proposals not requiring a panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify, with approval from the Selection Officials, which proposals do not require or are not eligible for a Review Panel (e.g., due to non-compliance with solicitation requirements or as noted for non-panel reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Note [2] for non-panel reviews and SPD-04 for unsolicited small-to-moderate budgets (§3.4.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Evaluations must be clear, concise, professional, and informative
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Evaluations shall, using professional tone and language, clearly and concisely provide constructive feedback to the proposers as well as sufficiently inform NASA’s selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Evaluations shall incorporate relevant findings from Individual Reviews as informed by discussion and label intrinsic merit findings as 'major' or 'minor' (§4.3.1–4.3.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation and treatment of External Reviewer findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Evaluations shall incorporate all relevant findings from the Individual Reviews, as informed by the Review Panel’s discussion. The Review Panel is authorized to accept/reject, in part or in full, or augment findings from the Individual Reviews of External Reviewers based on their discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Evaluation findings on intrinsic merit shall be labeled 'major' or 'minor' based on relative importance to the Panel Rating (§4.3.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Rating calculation and minimum reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Ratings should be the median of the Individual Ratings of the Panel Reviewers. A minimum of three unconflicted and unbiased Panel Reviewers shall contribute to the Panel Rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More reviewers may be needed to provide competent evaluations and remain in compliance; Program Officers must report any deviations to the Selection Official (§4.3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of non-rating comments and NASA-only considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that do not contribute to Panel Ratings, but may be of interest to the proposers, shall be in a section separate from any part of the Panel Evaluation that contributes to any Panel Rating. Comments about programmatic or other considerations that should not be visible to proposers shall be in a section addressed to NASA only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic considerations (e.g., priorities, balance) should be kept separate and, if sensitive, not visible to proposers (§4.3.4–4.3.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval chain for Panel Evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Evaluations shall be approved by at least the Primary Reviewer, Panel Chair, and Program Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final approval of Panel Evaluations must be made by a Civil Servant or IPA when applicable (§4.3.6, §3.4.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on post-panel editing of Panel Evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Officer shall only edit Panel Evaluations after the panel meeting to remove inappropriate language or correct erroneous content, with the overall scope of changes approved by the Selection Official. Formatting and grammatical corrections are allowed without approval by the Selection Official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive scope changes after panel require Selection Official approval (§4.3.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Panel Evaluations and Selection Decisions to proposers
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Officers shall ensure that each proposer is provided their Panel Evaluation and the Selection Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the GCAM on minimum requirements for Notices of Intent; debriefs and reconsideration requests handled per SPD-09 (§4.4.1, §4.4.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status notifications when selection delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: If Selection Decisions have not been provided to proposers within 150 days of the proposal due date, the Program Officer shall provide status notifications to proposers with conservative estimates of when selections are anticipated, every 60 days thereafter until Selection Decisions are delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of significant delay, Panel Evaluations may be provided prior to selections but must be provided no later than 6 weeks before next due date or one-year anniversary for no-due-date programs (§4.4.2–4.4.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Recommendations documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection Recommendations and Selection Decisions shall be documented in accordance with SPD-08.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection Recommendation must be prepared by a Civil Servant or IPA; Program Officer shall present Recommendation package to Selection Official (§3.4.10, §4.5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted additional considerations for Selection Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection Recommendations should be based on Panel Evaluations; however Program Officers may take into account other considerations, such as programmatic priorities, balance across subdisciplines/methodologies, support of innovative high-risk research, representation of breadth and diversity of the research community (as permitted by law), affordability issues, and other factors such as evidence for lack of progress, uncosted funds, or non-compliance with prior SMD grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programmatic considerations should be documented and, if not visible to proposers, placed in NASA-only sections of selection documentation (§4.5.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer shall not change Panel Ratings after panel meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Officer shall not change any Panel Ratings after the panel meeting, but instead provide in the selection documents any rationale needed to explain the Selection Recommendation (e.g., why a proposal is recommended over one with a higher Panel Rating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any explanations/rationales must be captured in selection documentation (SPD-08) (§4.5.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Official may differ from Program Officer but must document rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The Selection Official may fully follow the Program Officer’s Selection Recommendations, or make different Selection Decisions. In either case, the rationales must be captured in the selection documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMD aims for transparency; decisions should be explainable to proposers or the larger science community where possible (§4.5.4–4.5.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling allegations of research misconduct during review
rubrics_metrics.description: All allegations of research misconduct (fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism) reported to or discovered by the Program Officer shall be reported to the NASA Office of the Inspector General for assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officers shall instruct Reviewers to continue evaluating proposals with alleged misconduct as presented and without bias due to the allegation (§4.2.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer instruction to produce non-consensus findings and avoid ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Officer shall explain to all Panel Reviewers that their role is to provide clear, concise, professional, and non-consensus findings on individual proposals without comparing proposals, rank ordering proposals, or providing selection recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Evaluations are non-consensus documents that compile individual reviews and reflect panel discussion, not rankings (§4.2.3, §2.1.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing on implicit bias and reporting issues affecting panel quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Officer shall brief all Panel Reviewers on implicit bias ahead of the panel meeting. Any issues that may affect quality, integrity, inclusivity, or professionalism shall be immediately reported to the Program Officer or Panel Official (or R&A Leads/SARA Team if appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upholding codes of conduct and addressing issues promptly sustains review quality (§4.2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-panel review requirements for proposals not discussed in panels
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposal was not discussed in a panel, the Program Officer shall provide to the proposer either a summary or a collection of the Individual Reviews from External Reviewers, edited to only contain content that contributes to the disposition of the proposal, and with best efforts to remove all erroneous or inappropriate content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The above requirements for conflicts of interest, confidentiality, quality of reviews, timing, feedback, and selection rationale/approval are also applicable to non-panel reviews (§Notes [2]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to binding two-step proposal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: In solicitations that use a binding two-step process where proposers are rejected at the first step, the requirements for timing, feedback, and selection rationale and approval are also applicable to the first-step decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing (§4.4.2, §4.4.3), feedback (§4.4.4), and selection rationale/approval (§4.5.1, §4.5.4, §4.5.5) apply to first-step decisions in two-step solicitations (Note [1]).
